ECG Analyzer integrates with Apple Health to unleash the greatest power of your Apple Watch ECG, by analyzing and calculating HRV out of your ECG data, one of the best metrics for physical fitness and overall health level.

With HRV trends you can learn your health level changes. A up hill trend means a better physical fitness level and a down hill indicates you should pay more attention to your overall health.

Things you can do about your ECG data -

2. Calculate HRV (using RMSSD)

So what is HRV?
HRV is a measure of your autonomic nervous system that is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform.

Although HRV manifests as a function of your heart rate, it actually originates from your nervous system. Your autonomic nervous system, which controls the involuntary aspects of your physiology, has two branches, parasympathetic (deactivating) and sympathetic (activating).

The parasympathetic branch (often referred to as “rest and digest”) handles inputs from internal organs, like digestion or your fingernails and hair growing. It causes a decrease in heart rate.

The sympathetic branch (often called “fight or flight”) reflects responses to things like stress and exercise, and increases your heart rate.

Heart rate variability comes from these two competing branches simultaneously sending signals to your heart. If your nervous system is balanced, your heart is constantly being told to beat slower by your parasympathetic system, and beat faster by your sympathetic system. This causes a fluctuation in your heart rate: HRV.

Obsessive-compulsive disorder, or OCD, is a mental health condition that affects people of all ages. People with OCD often engage in compulsive behaviors, such as excessive hand-washing, to relieve their anxiety. However, these behaviors only temporarily ease the anxiety and often end up causing more distress in the long run.
Symptoms of OCD
The symptoms of OCD can vary from person to person. Some common symptoms include:
● Intrusive, unwanted thoughts (obsessions)
● Repetitive behaviors or mental acts (compulsions)
● Avoidance of situations or objects that trigger obsessions or compulsions
● Excessive hand-washing, cleaning, or grooming

What Can This App Do For Me? 
The OCD Screening Test app is specifically developed to give you a general sense of if your symptoms align with OCD symptoms. It is not a diagnostic test, and you should always consult with your doctor before making any decisions based on information given in this app. The OCD Screening Test utilizes the widely used Yale Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale to gauge your symptoms and determine if they align with those of OCD. The Test also allows you to save your results via a graph and chart that can show trends in your results over time. 

FAQ About OCD - 

How Is OCD Different From Being Neat And Organized?
OCD is different from being neat and organized in that it is a mental health condition that causes significant distress and interferes with a person’s ability to function in daily life. People with OCD often have obsessions, or intrusive thoughts, about dirt, germs, and other contaminants. These obsessions can lead to compulsions, or repetitive behaviors, such as excessive hand-washing.
 
While people who are neat and organized may prefer orderliness, but they do not feel the same level of distress or interference with daily life that people with OCD experience. Additionally, neat and organized people do not typically have obsessions associated with OCD. 
 
How Is OCD Treated?
OCD can be treated with the help of therapy, whereas some other treatments are also effective in this regard. All these remedies are given below:
 
1. Response Prevention Therapy
One type of therapy that is particularly effective for treating OCD is exposure and response prevention therapy (ERP). ERP is a type of cognitive-behavioral therapy that involves gradually exposing the person to their fear and then teaching them how to respond in a healthy way that does not involve engaging in their compulsive behavior.
2. Medications
In some cases, medications may also be prescribed to help treat OCD. Commonly prescribed medications include antidepressants, anti-anxiety medications, and antipsychotics. Medications can be an effective treatment for OCD when combined with therapy. People with OCD should always consult a mental health professional to determine if medication is right for them.
3. Therapist Consultation
If you are experiencing symptoms of OCD, it is important to consult with a mental health professional to discuss your treatment options. A therapist can help you identify your triggers and work with you to develop a customized treatment plan that meets your needs.
4. Self-Care
There are also several things that you can do on your own to help manage your OCD symptoms. These self-care strategies include :
• Identifying and challenging your negative thoughts
• Practicing relaxation techniques
• Avoiding triggers that exacerbate your symptoms
• Exercising regularly
• Getting enough sleep
 
OCD is a treatable condition, but it often requires a combination of therapy and medication to be effectively managed. Living with OCD can be difficult, but there are treatments available that can help you manage your symptoms and improve your quality of life. If you are struggling with OCD, contact a mental health professional for help. Always consult a doctor or mental health professional in case of severe symptoms first.
